security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from educational security examples that are explicitly labeled unsafe or paired with safer alternatives. The only confirmed risks are the shipped Bash audit scripts and filesystem scanning behavior, which are legitimate defensive capabilities but require user awareness before execution.

remediation.issue: Executable audit scripts are included with the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Keep script execution opt-in and document that dependency tools may access package metadata or network services when users run them.

remediation.issue: Educational examples include intentionally unsafe patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Keep WRONG and CORRECT labels prominent so agents do not copy vulnerable examples into production code.

remediation.issue: The grep scanner reads files from a user-supplied directory.
remediation.suggestion: Continue quoting directory arguments and remind users to run scans only on repositories they are authorized to inspect.

content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss common web application risks and inconsistent implementation details. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused OWASP guidance, safe examples, and local audit helpers.
actual_capabilities: Explains OWASP Top 10 risks with prevention checklists.
Provides secure examples for input validation, output encoding, authentication, and authorization.
Documents cryptography patterns for hashing, signatures, key derivation, and key storage.
Lists recommended HTTP security headers and framework examples.
Includes shell scripts for local dependency and grep-based security checks.
limitations: Does not replace a full penetration test or threat model.
The scripts rely on local tools that may not be installed.
Pattern-based scans can produce false positives and miss context-specific flaws.
Examples require adaptation before use in production systems.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request for common web risks
use_cases.description: Use the OWASP checklist to check access control, injection, authentication, secrets, and SSRF risks before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare secure implementation guidance
use_cases.description: Use the reference examples to guide safe authentication, headers, and cryptography choices during feature design.

use_cases.title: Run a quick local dependency audit
use_cases.description: Use the included scripts to identify vulnerable packages and suspicious code patterns in a local project.

prompt_templates.title: Check one feature for OWASP risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature for OWASP Top 10 risks. Focus on access control, input validation, output encoding, and secrets handling.

prompt_templates.title: Compare code to secure examples
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my authentication and session handling code against this skill. Identify gaps and suggest concrete secure changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a targeted security audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare review work for a service
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security audit checklist for this service using the OWASP, authentication, cryptography, and headers references in this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Triage scan output with context
prompt_templates.prompt: I ran the local security scan. Triage these findings, separate true risks from false positives, and recommend prioritized remediation.

output_examples.input: Review this endpoint for access control and injection risks.
output: Checks whether authorization is enforced server-side.
Flags string-built queries and recommends parameterized queries.
Suggests logging failed authorization without exposing sensitive data.

output_examples.input: Help me harden HTTP response headers for a production app.
output: Recommends CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
Explains which directives need application-specific values.
Suggests testing headers with a scanner after deployment.
Separates dev-only packages from production exposure.
Suggests upgrades, workarounds, or package replacement when needed.

best_practices: Use the references as a checklist, then verify behavior in the running application.
Treat every scanner result as a lead that needs code context before remediation.
Adapt examples to your framework and security requirements before production use.
anti_patterns: Copying wrong examples that are shown only to illustrate vulnerabilities.
Relying only on grep scans for security approval.
Adding broad CSP exceptions without confirming the required sources.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Python projects?
faq.answer: No. It is language-agnostic, but many examples use Python and JavaScript.

faq.question: Can it run security scans automatically?
faq.answer: It includes shell scripts for local scans, but a user or agent must run them intentionally.

faq.question: Does it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and lightweight checks, not complete dynamic or manual testing.

faq.question: Why are some examples intentionally insecure?
faq.answer: They show unsafe patterns next to safer alternatives so reviewers can recognize real issues.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets safely?
faq.answer: It recommends environment variables or secrets managers and warns against committed secrets.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for security review workflows.
